To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the blockade of serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT) 2A receptors in ventromedial (vm) prefrontal cortex selectively attenuates the reinstatement of cocaine seeking elicited by cocaine-associated cues, but not by cocaine priming.
blockade of 5HT2A receptors in ventromedial, but not anterior cingulate, cortex selectively attenuates the reinstatement of cocaine seeking induced by cocaine-paired cues.
M100907 (1.0 or 1.0 μg) infused directly in the ventromedian prefrontal cortex decreased cue-elicitted reinstatement of cocaine self-administration in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of addiction.

identifying the neural circuitry involved in the incentive motivational effects that are associated with exposure to cocaine-paired cues, and with identifying the neural mechanisms that are involved in the reinstatement of cocaine self-administration that is elicited by exposure to cocaine-pared cues.
the neurochemical mechanisms underlying the motivational effects of drug cues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5-HT2a receptors in the medial PFC play a role in cue reactivity and cue-induced reinstatement of cocaine seeking behavior.
the blockade of the 5-HT(2A) receptor in the mPFC attenuates reinstatement elicited by drug cues, but not reinstatement elicited through drug priming.
the blockade of the 5-HT(2A) receptor in the vmPCC selectively attenuated the incentive motivational effects induced by cocaine-paired cues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5-HT system plays a key role in cue- but not cocaine-induced reinstatement of cocaine seeking behavior.
5-HT2a receptors in the vm PFC are involved in cue-elicited, but not drug-elicited cocaine seeking.

5-HT2C receptors are involved in the initiation of cocaine seeking, whereas 5-HT2ARs are involved in the maintenance of cocaine seeking, and 5-HT2BRs are involved in both the initiation and maintenance of cocaine seeking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vmPFC is an important brain region in the control of cue-induced cocaine-seeking behavior.
5-HT2ARs in the vmPFR play a role in cue-elicited, but not cocaine-primed, reinstatement of drug seeking.
M100907 may prove useful as a therapeutic agent to reduce cocaine craving.
